page: Microsoft Azure D4s_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine hypervised via Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor running at a base clock of 2.6 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled (2 threads per core). Memory capacity stands at 16.0 GB RAM, adhering to a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per vCPU). The CPU features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512 (F and VNNI), and AES-NI.

The D4s_v4 instance does not include bundled local storage or dedicated graphics hardware (0 GPUs), requiring workloads to rely exclusively on remote Azure managed storage solutions. Across compute benchmarks, performance leans toward entry to lower-mid tier levels. Stress-ng returned scores of 1410.29 for single-core and 3705.66 for multi-core compute, both placing in the bottom 25% of cloud systems. Geekbench yielded a single-core score of 1171.0 and a multi-core score of 2604.0. In instruction-heavy operations, clang software compilation scored 3504.0, while ray tracing reached 3111.0.

Memory subsystem benchmarks show uncached read throughput of 17.74 GB/sec and uncached write speeds of 15.28 GB/sec, placing memory throughput in the lower brackets. In contrast, PassMark memory performance placed in the middle 50% with a score of 2084.17. Data operations measured 3.41 million operations per second for Redis SET requests and a PassMark database score of 1481.95. For lightweight language tasks, small 135M model text generation executed at 94.04 tokens per second, though prompt processing was comparatively limited at 274.89 tokens per second. Static web serving throughput reached 4.01 GB/sec.

Positioned as a balanced resource tier, the D4s_v4 prioritizes predictable resource allocation over raw throughput. Because it lacks local ephemeral NVMe disks, users trade off local I/O performance for flexibility with remote disks. The hardware profile is suitable for standard enterprise web serving, mid-range application servers, background task queues, and general business software environments that require balanced memory and compute without demanding peak floating-point throughput.
